En una reacción química los átomos no se: In a chemical reaction atoms are neither created nor destroyed: they are only rearranged. Balancing it means finding the stoichiometric coefficients, the numbers in front of each formula, so that there are the same atoms of each element in the reactants as in the products. In an ionic reaction, the total charge must also be the same on both sides.
Se pone una incógnita delante de cada es: An unknown is put in front of each species ($a$, $b$, $c$…) and one equation is written per element. For the combustion of propane, $a$ C₃H₈ + $b$ O₂ → $c$ CO₂ + $d$ H₂O, those for carbon, hydrogen and oxygen are:
Es un sistema homogéneo con una incógnit: It is a homogeneous system with one free unknown: give the value $a = 1$, solve for the others ($c = 3$, $d = 4$, $b = 5$) and, if fractions come out, multiply everything by the least common multiple of the denominators. The coefficients are left as whole numbers and as small as possible.
En reacciones sencillas se suele ajustar: In simple reactions it is usually balanced by eye: first the metals, then the nonmetals, then hydrogen and finally oxygen. The algebraic method always reaches the same result and also works when inspection gets complicated. For redox reactions, the ion-electron method separates oxidation and reduction, but the final balancing is the same as the system gives.
Ecuación iónica neta y tipo de reacción: Net ionic equation and reaction type
Si la reacción tiene sales, ácidos o bas: If the reaction has salts, acids or bases, the working adds the complete ionic equation, removes the spectator ions (those that appear the same on both sides) and leaves the net ionic equation: what really changes. Dissolved strong electrolytes (soluble salts, strong acids and strong bases) are written as ions; solids, gases, water and weak electrolytes, whole. If you do not write the states, they are assumed with the solubility rules: salts of alkali metals, of ammonium, nitrates and acetates are soluble; chlorides, bromides and iodides too, except those of silver and lead; sulfates, except those of barium, strontium, lead and calcium; carbonates, phosphates, sulfides and hydroxides are insoluble except those of the alkali metals. You can write the states yourself, such as AgNO3(aq), and they take precedence over the rules. The reaction is also classified (synthesis, decomposition, combustion, neutralization, precipitation, displacement).
Si la ecuación admite más de un ajuste i: If the equation admits more than one independent balancing (for example, C + O₂ → CO + CO₂), it is actually the sum of several reactions and the independent balancings are shown so you can separate them. If it admits none, a substance is usually missing (water, H⁺ or OH⁻ in an ionic reaction) or a formula is misspelled.
